title: Short Stirling R9329
cause_of_loss: Fired on by shore defences crossing the coast near Plymouth on return; crashed 8 miles inland at 03:25
memorial_details:
Rectangular granite freestanding stone of remembrance. Lettering is carved in black.

A granite pillar was set up at the crash site in 2011.
inscription: STIRLING BOMBER OF/ 149 SQDN RAF/ CRASHED HERE WITH/ THE LOSS OF/ 7 AIRCREW ON THE/ 21ST AUGUST 1942/ CREW:/ (Names)/ WE WILL REMEMBER THEM

sources.title: Facebook post by Daran Walker (RAF Bomber Command Memorials group)
Gibhill Wood crash site of Short Stirling bomber R9329

narrative:
Short Stirling R9329 of 149 Squadron left RAF Lakenheath at 2045 on 20 August 1942 to lay mines off the Gironde estuary near Bordeaux. It crashed in Gibhill Wood, near Cornwood on Dartmoor, at 0325 on 21 August 1942. All seven crew died. The navigator's log survived; its last entry, about ten minutes before the crash, read 03.15 completely lost.

The sources disagree on why it came down. Dartmoor Explorations reports that the RAF accident report found the aircraft probably damaged by ground defences over France and that it flew into rising ground and caught fire. IBCC says it is believed to have been hit by anti-aircraft fire over Plymouth on the return. Dartmoor Explorations also notes a suggestion of friendly fire over Plymouth from the brother of one crewman, with no conclusive evidence.

The pilot was Pilot Officer Geoffrey Ernest Robertson, aged 25, of the RAFVR. IBCC records him as a Pilot Officer; Dartmoor Explorations lists him as a Sergeant. The other six were all sergeants: Jenkins (22), Simpson (26), Harris (20), Nicholson (21, forward gunner), Clarke (25) and Bond (19), according to Dartmoor Explorations.
community_connection: Four local men, Gordon Fowell, Alan Graham, Peter Sandover and Ian Stone, began planning it in 2009. It was unveiled at a dedication service by David Nicholson, nephew of Sgt Lawrence Nicholson.

crew.name: P E J Jenkins (Peter Edward James Jenkins)
